newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 28.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on November 28. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Indonesian Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad told a parliamentary commission on Wednesday that the country's current account deficit was becoming uncontrollable. The deficit is expected to be four percent of GDP for fiscal 1996/7, up from two percent in 1994/5 and 3.4 percent in 1995/6.

Foreign hotel chains that operate in Indonesia must set up local joint-venture companies by the turn of the century and reduce expatriates in top management to no more than three people, the country's Director General of Tourism said yesterday.

Abdurrahaman Wahid, leader of the 30-million strong Nahdlatul Ulama (NU), will soon meet Research and Technology Minister Jusuf Habibie, who is also head of an influential group of Islamic scholars. The meeting will strengthen links between the two Moslem associations, which are perceived to have a distant relationship, an NU member said yesterday.

First Pacific Company Ltd of Hong Kong is to acquire a stake in Indonesian mobile cellular telecommunications operator PT Metro Selular through its subsidiary Asia Link B.V. Asia Link, a wholly owned subsidiary of First Pacific, signed an agreement on Wednesday to take a 35 percent stake in the enlarged and outstanding share capital of PT Metro Selular for $147 million.
